provenance.note: consumes_cavity_depth is false: the fan is assumed to vent OUTWARD through the cover rather than sitting inside the cavity depth. This is the single most consequential assumption in the register. If the fan must sit inside, the blank fails by 6.55 mm. No source states which. See conflict CONF-FAN-INTRUSION.

Deliberately NOT placed in any cavity plan. The source sites it 'under Pi 5', where its 3.5 mm would fit inside the Pi's 6 mm standoff gap and consume no additional depth or plan area. That is an assumption, not a derivation, so the part is registered and left unplaced rather than modelled falsely. See conflict CONF-NVME-PLACEMENT.

cavity_plans.description: Rear-access electronics pod housing the Pi 5 and HiFiBerry DAC+ADC side by side, with a lid-mounted cooling fan

provenance.note: Layout ruled side_by_side by the owner on 2026-07-26. The source declares stacked_vertical with total_height_mm 76.0, which cannot fit any guitar-plausible blank: stacked, the assembly is 58 mm before lid clearance, against a 44.45 mm body. No stated length or width exists in any source, so both are derived. min_floor 8.0 mm is an engineering estimate awaiting structural review.

cavity_plans.description: Rear-access pocket for the Teensy 4.1 I/O coprocessor, sited near the neck pickup for a short analog lead

provenance.note: luthiers-toolbox states the same 70 x 25 x 20 mm pocket, so the two sources agree here.

cavity_plans.description: Chamber for the 4x 18650 pack and BMS, with power routed to the pod via the spine channel

provenance.note: Modelled as its own chamber because the battery is a separate cavity in sg-spec. Its plan POSITION is unresolved: sg-spec sites it in a bass chamber that a solid body does not have. Depth and footprint are still valid regardless of where it lands. See conflict CONF-BATTERY-PLACEMENT.

provenance.note: SMART-GUITAR-CAVITY-GEOMETRY-1. Dated read-only snapshot: values were copied here so the derivation stays reproducible if the source repositories change, which they are expected to.

notes: INTERNAL physical geometry record. Contains no cost, price, or manufacturing-time fields by design.

Every cavity dimension in the paired geometry record is DERIVED from this register. Nothing downstream reads a stated cavity dimension, which is why a stale note like 'total_height_mm: 76.0' cannot propagate.
stated_* fields exist only so the derivation can be compared against the source specs. They are never inputs.

The source scan behind this register was BOUNDED and is not exhaustive. It covered sg-spec, luthiers-toolbox instrument_geometry, and tap_tone_pi hardware docs. string_master_v.4.0 was not fully searched. Absence of a conflict record is not evidence that no conflict exists.

min_floor_mm is 8.0 on every cavity: an engineering estimate, not a structural calculation. The pod sits in the lower bout near the control cavity and the battery routing, so the real minimum should come from a structural review under string tension.
The derived pod footprint is a LOWER BOUND. The Hi-Z buffered splitter is required by the canonical signal chain and has no dimensions anywhere, so it could not be included.

This record derives cavity SIZE only. It does not validate cavity POSITION against the body outline, so it cannot detect two cavities colliding in plan or a cavity breaching the perimeter. Plan-level collision checking needs the traced outline and is out of scope. CONF-OPPOSED-FACE-WEB is a concrete instance of what that omission hides.

Pickups, pickup routes, the neck pocket, the bridge, the control cavity, and the output jack are NOT modelled here. This register covers the embedded-electronics cavities only: the pod, the Teensy pocket, and the battery chamber. Pickup disagreements are recorded as conflicts (CONF-PICKUP-TYPE, CONF-PICKUP-ROUTE-DIMS) but no pickup dimension is derived or fit-checked.

Because top-face routes are excluded, the derived body thickness is a LOWER BOUND in a second way: it accounts only for back-face cavity depth plus floor, never for a top-face route cutting toward the same plane from the other side.
